criteria.evidence: The fragment model preserves wire identity and ordering, but its heterogeneous interface vector is not reconciled with §3.3's definition of a register as wires of one class.
criteria.change: In §3.3 state: “A register contains an ordered wire vector with a resolved class per wire; a single class abbreviates a homogeneous vector.”

criteria.evidence: The X witness is correct and no gate semantics change. The interacting qreg.concat rule permits distinct live operands without requiring equal classes, while the register definition remains homogeneous.
criteria.change: In §3.3 state: “qreg.concat concatenates the operands' wire and class vectors without moving wires; qreg.slice selects the corresponding sub-vectors.”

criteria.evidence: Fragments introduce no quantum operation, alias, allocation or lifetime. The exact X sequence maps 0,1,2,3 to 3,2,1,0, and its adjoint restores every input.
criteria.change: No correction required. Optionally add to §9.4: “Fragmentation is descriptive metadata and introduces no gate, measurement or routing operation.”

criteria.evidence: §§8.2–8.4 and §11 support the stated sequential time 2, occupancy 2 per class and peak 1 per class. The proposed topology equality, complete partition and no-double-charge rules are precise.
criteria.change: No correction required. To strengthen the example, add under Conformance: “For region[1,2], offsets 0,1,2,3 denote (cell,bit) pairs (0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1).”

criteria.evidence: The B5 defect is real: §9.4 supplies one class per complete slot, while §11 supplies per-bit placements. The proposed alternatives and validation rules repair that encoding. The required mixed-fat-object application statement is absent.
criteria.change: Append to §9.4: “In a mixed fat object, B5 frames describe device-region invocations in embedded ISA objects; native host modules require neither B5 frames nor ISA conversion.”

criteria.evidence: I reproduced the INDEX finite-check prefix and independently checked the basis map, inverse, resource totals and region flattening. The note accurately distinguishes arithmetic checks from unexecuted schema/target validation. Its additional controlled case needs a larger target.
criteria.change: In Conformance specify a third control vertex of class C, capacity 1, edges to both target vertices and exact controlled-X support; expected output is t for control 0 and t XOR 3 for control 1.

criteria.evidence: The proposal preserves source slots and permits target-driven heterogeneous placement without manufacturing capacity. However, neither the note nor INDEX states how this certificate extension is used by the native-host-plus-device mixed fat object required by the standing check.
criteria.change: Add the mixed-fat-object rule in B2, including device CC launch and the register binding that makes the fragmented slot reachable.

criteria.evidence: The fragment rules are implementable and retain the homogeneous shorthand. Under INDEX's authorized in-version route, §9.2 excludes certificates from object identity; recipes and ordinals are untouched. I also reproduced the published frame, topology-target and reference-catalog hashes. Consumer migration could be stated more directly.
criteria.change: In Release and route state: “For the authorized in-version K publication, consumers upgrade to accept both B5 alternatives; older consumers reject fragments under §9.1, and producers must not disguise heterogeneous slots as homogeneous records.”

blocking.section: Recommended exact spec diff; ISA §3.3 interacting with §§9.4 and 10
blocking.problem: The proposed heterogeneous frame is not reconciled with the runtime register model. §3.3 explicitly defines a register as “n device-resident wires of one class” and records its singular class. Yet qreg.concat requires only distinct live non-view registers and preserves their wires without movement. On the witness target, allocate qA with one A wire and qB with one B wire, concatenate them, and bind the result to split's wire[2] slot. The concatenation satisfies its stated preconditions and produces the proposed [A,B] placement, but violates the unchanged register definition. Rejecting it, relabelling a bit, and preserving the heterogeneous result cannot all implement the same amended machine. This is a direct interaction with the new class-vector contract, not a denial of the placement-level B5 defect.
blocking.fix: Extend the diff to §3.3: “A register contains an ordered vector of device-resident wires with a resolved class per wire. A single class abbreviates a homogeneous vector. qreg.new retains its requested-class allocation rule. qreg.concat accepts differing operand classes and concatenates their wire/class vectors without movement; qreg.slice inherits the selected sub-vectors. Free and reversal records preserve and restore the complete vector. Region binding preserves that vector, which the selected §9.4 frame must describe.” Add the A/B concatenation witness: the joined register has classes [A,B], split maps 0,1,2,3 to 3,2,1,0, and reversal restores the original wire ordering, classes and handle states. A separately specified heterogeneous register/view mechanism is another viable route; extending the existing qreg model is the smaller repair.

blocking.section: Hashes, catalog and consumers; Recommended exact spec diff
blocking.problem: The proposal changes certificate layout but contains no mixed-fat-object application statement. INDEX's general assertion that North Star capabilities remain does not state which embedded objects receive these frames or how native host code reaches the fragmented device slot. This fails the council's explicit standing check for certificate-layout changes.
blocking.fix: Append to §9.4: “In a mixed fat object, these descriptors apply to device-region invocations in the embedded ISA objects, using the certificate's existing object, closure and invocation bindings. Native host modules remain native and require neither ISA conversion nor B5 frame records. Native host code launches a device CC entry through §10; that entry may concatenate homogeneous registers under §3.3 and bind the resulting ordered class vector to one source interface slot. The slot's fragments describe that binding without splitting its signature. Native process entry, argv/environment and host-library execution remain outside this device-frame inventory.” For the witness, the native host launches a device CC wrapper that joins A[1] and B[1] and invokes split with the single mut:0 slot.

suggestions: Conformance vectors: state that the controlled positive case uses vertices 0:A, 1:B, 2:C, capacity 1 each, edges [0,2] and [1,2], and exact controlled-X entries of duration 1. With sequential execution and unit rates, time is 2, each class has occupancy 2 and peak 1; the control is preserved and t maps to t XOR (3·control). The original two-vertex target has no room for the extra control.

Release and route / INDEX publication rules: explicitly select the recommended authorized in-version K route and state: “Existing homogeneous certificates retain their encoding; updated consumers accept fragments; older consumers reject the unknown field. Consumers must upgrade before processing fragmented certificates. Source, schedule, target and ref@0.9 bytes remain unchanged when only the certificate descriptor changes.” A full-version publication remains viable, but must instead regenerate affected envelopes and consumer pins as INDEX explains.
path_to_accept: First reconcile §3.3's register/class and reversal rules with heterogeneous vectors and add the concatenation witness. Then add the explicit mixed-fat-object application statement. The fragment encoding itself can remain as proposed.
summary: The B5 defect, fragment encoding, arithmetic and conditional hash claims are sound. Two interacting omissions prevent acceptance: the homogeneous runtime-register definition and the mandatory mixed-fat-object application statement.
